clue.text: Increased cut by a quarter

parts.note: W, west, is one of the four quarters or points of the compass
to be axed is to be cut

explanation.surface: Something was raised by a quarter, or perhaps trimmed by a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Increased' looks like a figure going up; it is the old verb wax, as the moon waxes. 'by' just sets the quarter beside the cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To wax is to grow, as the moon does, so waxed means grew larger.

clue.text: Field worker who never gives a clear answer

definitions.meaning: a farm hand who trims and lays hedges round fields

definitions.text: who never gives a clear answer
definitions.meaning: someone who hedges, avoiding committing themselves

explanation.definitionFit: One who tends hedgerows; also one who evades by hedging his bets in speech.

clue.text: Criminal upset the head of state?

parts.note: to offend someone is to upset them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen as British head of state

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker who has annoyed the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the crossword convention for the Queen, who heads the British state.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or lawbreaker is a criminal; as nouns the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Inclined not to start the washing

indicators.note: the word for the washing loses its opening letter, so it does not start

parts.note: doing the washing is cleaning

explanation.surface: Someone is disinclined to begin the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' reads as 'minded to'; it is the definition, meaning tilted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tilted or sloping is leaning, as a tower can lean.

clue.text: Almost faint — abnormal tailless rodent of ill-repute!

indicators.note: abnormal says the letters gathered are put into an irregular order
almost the whole word faint, stopping short of its last letter
the rodent loses its tail, its final letter

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A swooning reaction to a strange mouse with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIN (faint without its T) plus MOUS (mouse without its E) are rearranged by 'abnormal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious, having a bad reputation, is what infamous means.

clue.text: Surrendered loudly after seeing coppers get up, and followed

indicators.note: after says the surrendered word follows the coppers
in a down clue, getting up means the coppers read from bottom to top

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, so coppers are CUs

indicators.note: loudly says the word for surrendered is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: ceded means surrendered, handed over

explanation.surface: Someone gave in noisily on seeing the police stand up, then came next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' turns CUS into SUC; 'loudly' makes CEDED sound as CEEDED. 'seeing' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to come after them, so succeeded means came next.

clue.text: Be like father and steal a 12 inch ruler

parts.note: to take something is to steal it
taken as written
twelve inches make a foot, abbreviated FT
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen as ruler

explanation.surface: Resembling your dad and pinching a foot-long ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests the measuring stick; it is the monarch ER. Twelve inches make a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Children who resemble a parent are said to take after them.

clue.text: Nose which is socially acceptable in heavyweights making a comeback

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other
making a comeback means the weights word is read backwards

parts.note: tons are heavy weights
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, in British usage

explanation.surface: Snooping among returning heavyweight boxers, socially accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns TONS into SNOT, and U goes 'in' it. U for upper-class is a British crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's snout is its projecting nose and mouth.

clue.text: Past bickering?

indicators.note: bickering letters quarrel and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Quarrelling that is over and done with.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a spat is a bit of bickering, here over.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty quarrel is a spat.

clue.text: Off-colour, in the main?

parts.note: off-colour means looking ill, green with seasickness; the main is the sea, so someone looking queasy at sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is a poetic word for the ocean; the answer is also a pale bluish-green colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale blue-green shade, here read as being green out on the ocean.

clue.text: One in position to fish

indicators.note: in says the numeral sits inside the position word

parts.note: a place is a position
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone waiting in place to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in position' reads as a person stationed; 'in' puts I inside PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaice is a flatfish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Network that's free after middle age

indicators.note: after says the free word follows the middle letter
the middle letter of the word age is taken

parts.note: to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A web of contacts that is liberated once you pass middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle age' looks like the time of life; it is the centre letter of 'age'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of lines, as in the national power grid.

clue.text: New ringtone is a gas!

indicators.note: new says the letters of the following word are made fresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: Excitement at a fresh phone tune, which is such fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a gas' means great fun; here 'gas' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is a gas, the main component of air: an example of the class.

clue.text: One has no experience of putting area on alarm

parts.note: in golf, the green is where you putt
a horn sounds an alarm

explanation.surface: A golfer new to the game honks a horn on the green.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf green is the short-grass area round the hole where players putt.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice, someone raw and untried, is a greenhorn.

clue.text: Alternatively a Conservative speech

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Or else, a Conservative politician's address.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of public speaking, eloquent formal address.

clue.text: 27 not prepared for attack

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made up, worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the answer to 27 across, a word for angry

explanation.surface: An angry person unready to launch an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not prepared' reads as unready, but 'not' is fodder and 'prepared' the anagram signal, mixing IRATE with NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear into someone is to attack them fiercely, an idiom.

clue.text: It is Susan's answer to a cold!

parts.note: 'tis is a contraction of it is
Sue is short for Susan, so Susan's is Sue's

explanation.surface: Susan's remedy for a sniffle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's pieces are a contraction and a pet name plus possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper handkerchiefs are the usual remedy for a runny nose with a chill, so the plural fits 'answer' as a collective.

clue.text: Where film is kept secretly

definitions.meaning: film for photographs sits inside a picture-taking device
in private, behind closed doors, as a court hearing held privately

explanation.definitionFit: Literally inside a photographic device; idiomatically a Latin legal term for in private session.

clue.text: Happy communicators, of late!

parts.note: a happy medium is a compromise; spiritualists communicate with the late, the dead, so these are communicators with the departed

explanation.walkthrough: 'of late' looks like 'recently' but means with the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualists who claim to pass messages from the dead are called mediums.

clue.text: Not to mention being terribly late and solitary

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of the next word are shaken badly out of order

parts.note: lone means solitary

explanation.surface: Someone running dreadfully behind time and on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' and 'solitary' sit together in the surface as a sad picture, but 'terribly' is the anagram signal working only on 'late'; 'being' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'let alone' means much less, never mind, introducing something even less likely.

clue.text: Horse race for which drunkard initially travelled south

indicators.note: the opening letter moves down to the bottom, south in a down clue

parts.note: a soak is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drunk went south for a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry south is the bottom, so the S of SOAK moves to the end. The Oaks is a classic English flat race for fillies at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is a famous English flat race run at Epsom.

clue.text: Groom's first of many eaten by horse

definitions.note: Groom is, the 's standing for is

indicators.note: eaten by says the letter goes inside the horse word

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy horse

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word many is taken

explanation.surface: A stable groom's first of many horses is eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a stable hand, fitting the horse; here it is a verb, to tidy hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom hair is to tidy it, which is what a comb does, as a verb.

clue.text: A household where people get on

parts.note: men are people
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: A home where the occupants rub along well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' suggests getting along; it means growing older.
explanation.definitionFit: Ménage is a French loanword for a domestic establishment or home.

clue.text: Delighted to be broadcasting

definitions.meaning: transmitting live on radio or television

explanation.definitionFit: Elated, as in walking on air; and being transmitted live on radio or television.

clue.text: Analyst's contract

definitions.meaning: an analyst is, the 's standing for is; slang for a psychiatrist

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a psychiatrist, short for head-shrinker; and to become smaller.

clue.text: Threatening explosive device in mint exploding

indicators.note: in says the device sits inside the other letters
exploding blows the letters of the word mint apart into a new order

parts.note: a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: A bomb inside a mint is about to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' scrambles MINT into IMNT, with MINE set 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something about to happen, looming, is imminent.

clue.text: Blackbeard, for example, lost his head, getting angry

indicators.note: the pirate loses his first letter, his head

parts.note: Blackbeard was a famous pirate

explanation.surface: The pirate Blackbeard, beheaded, became furious.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackbeard was the notorious 18th-century pirate Edward Teach.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious or very cross is a synonym for irate.

clue.text: Confusion on oil rig — mob running riot

indicators.note: running riot says the letters charge about out of their order

explanation.surface: Chaos on a drilling platform as a mob rampages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running riot' rearranges OIL RIG and MOB together.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a messy, complicated situation or tangle.
